STAGE-WIDE — read before touching anything.

ORDERING. KS3.2 → KS3.3 → KS3.1 → KS3.4 → KS3.5. KS3.2 must land before KS3.1 and KS3.5 or every plan those checkpoints write is written by the destroying editor. KS3.2 and KS3.3 both rewrite docs/plan-config.md's opening paragraph (lines 9-12) — sequence them, do not run them as parallel lanes. KS3.5 is a cut line: deliver last, park rather than half-ship.

CROSS-STAGE. KS1.4 lands doctor's plan-semantics lints (gate-command path probe, checkpoint-id-vs-tracker cross-check, hook dry-run, plan drift, argv-length 8191 check, brace sweep, escalation-token sweep). KS3.1's "doctor-clean by construction" and KS3.4's doctor + escalation legs build on it — if KS1.4 has not landed, implement against today's doctor and re-verify after. KS3.4's escalation-block leg and KS1.4's HUMAN-token sweep must be ONE implementation. KS2.1 makes bare `conductor` a default command; `preflight` must survive that routing. KS10.2 re-pins docs/cli.md and docs/plan-config.md — leave both extendable.

HOW TO EXERCISE (trap 2). The `conductor` on PATH is the PUBLISHED engine driving this run; it does not have your changes. Always `dotnet run --project src/Conductor -- VERB ...`. Testing a new verb through the PATH shim only proves the published engine lacks it. Exception by design: `conductor task --done` claims go through the PATH copy, because they target the driving run.

NEVER AIM AT THIS REPO (traps 0, 1, 4). No run-control verb (run, pause, resume, abort, approve, plan set, plan reload, plan add-stage, plan import, goto, skip, retry-stage, rollback, kill) may target C:/code/conductor or plans/karvansara/core.plan.json — that file is the live annotated plan and the exact artifact KS3.2 exists to protect. Every live proof spawns YOUR build against a scratch repo under the temp directory with its own tiny plan, its own state dir and its own port. Pass -p explicitly on every verb and clear CONDUCTOR_PLAN in any shell you spawn. Never run tools/install.ps1 or overwrite the published engine.

GATES (from the plan — run these, never the tools/gates battery, which rebuilds the running engine, trap 7 / bug 16):
  engine-fast:  dotnet build Conductor.slnx -clp:ErrorsOnly
  engine-full:  dotnet test Conductor.slnx
  face-fast:    cmd /c "cd /d C:\code\conductor\face-go && go build ./... && go vet ./..."
  face-full:    cmd /c "cd /d C:\code\conductor\face-go && go test ./..."
KS3 is engine-only; no face-go change is expected. The handoff carries the FULL-suite number, never a filtered one — `dotnet test --filter` is for the inner loop only.

ARCHITECTURE CEILING IS ENFORCED. tests/Conductor.Tests/architecture-baseline.json: lineCeiling 500, maxTypesPerFile 3, filesOverLineCeiling {} (zero approved violations). DoctorCommand.cs is already 468 lines — KS3.3's inert-key check and any KS3.4 doctor reuse go in a NEW partial, following the repo's convention (DoctorCommand.State.cs, DoctorCommand.Update.cs).

THE TWO VERB PINS. A new top-level verb is three edits: Program.cs (`AddCommand<X>("verb")`, not `.IsHidden()`), CompletionCommand.Verbs, and docs/cli.md. K7_2DocsVerbCoverageTests.CliReference_NamesEveryShippedVerb scans Program.cs against docs/cli.md; B11_2Tests.Completion_ContainsAllRegisteredVerbs_Exhaustive scans it against both completion scripts. `plan new` is a SUBverb and trips neither — but PlanCommand's `_ => PrintPlanSummary` default currently swallows unrecognised subverbs silently; fix that in KS3.1.

COMMENT PRESERVATION, THE REAL CONSTRAINT. System.Text.Json has no comment-preserving writer — JsonSerializer, JsonDocument and JsonNode all drop trivia (PlanConfig.JsonOpts sets ReadCommentHandling = Skip). `plan set` round-trips through JsonNode (PlanSetCommand.cs:44-169); `plan add-stage` goes through PlanConfig.Save() (PlanConfig.cs:176-181), which re-serialises the whole object and therefore also materialises defaults — that is the separate half of the trap ("adding one stage changed three unrelated things"). Sanctioned fixes: a hand-rolled text-span editor over the raw file, or an owned `header` field. Encoding gotcha: plan set writes UTF8 WITHOUT BOM, PlanConfig.Save writes WITH BOM.

MUTATINGLANES, PRECISELY. PlanConfig.MutatingLanes (PlanConfig.cs:93) has ZERO readers in src/ — verified by `grep -rn "\.MutatingLanes" src/`. But MutatingLaneConfig (src/Conductor.Core/Models/AnalysisLaneConfig.cs:29) and MutatingLaneRunner ARE live: LaneCoordinator.FollowupEntryToMutatingLane (:247) builds them from .conductor/followups.md after a stage confirms. On the removal branch, remove the PLAN PROPERTY only, retire B12_3Tests.PlanConfig_MutatingLanes_DefaultsEmpty in the same commit, and strip the key from plans/conductor-sarban-core.plan.json:223 and plans/conductor-sarban-face.plan.json:239 (PlanSetCommandTests.EveryKeyInEveryShippedPlanResolves scans plans/*.plan.json at top level only) plus plans/karvan/core.plan.json:225 and plans/karvan/lanes.plan.json:213.

TEMPLATES AND PROSE (traps 8, 9). Any template written under a plan's templatesDir is validated for unresolved placeholders; a stray {token} kills the engine at first render with a stderr-only refusal. Sweep every generated template — only real placeholder names, and a doubled brace emits a literal one. Stage notes and promptExtra are refused at load for the same reason (PlanConfig.ValidateProse). Never put the literal escalation token (the word HUMAN followed by a colon) in a tracker handoff block, a generated tracker template, or preflight's own output — the match is a plain substring, it parks the run and floods Telegram.

DOCS-MATCH-REALITY IS THE HOUSE IDIOM. SF7_1DocsMatchRealityTests is a partial class split across five files (.cs, .Backlog, .FieldNotes, .Ledgers, .Skill) with RepoRoot()/Doc() helpers. Add KS3.3's plan-config pin as a NEW partial (SF7_1DocsMatchRealityTests.PlanKeys.cs) that DERIVES its expectation from PlanKeySchema/PlanConfig reflection — never a hand-typed key list; that is the exact rot this suite exists to stop. Prove each new pin RED on a seeded stale doc before it counts.

TEST PLACEMENT. Engine tests are flat in tests/Conductor.Tests/ named by checkpoint (KS0_1CatalogueRepairTests.cs, KS0_3ShadowBuildTests.cs …) — follow that: KS3_1PlanNewTests.cs, KS3_2PlanEditPreservesTests.cs, KS3_3SchemaHonestyTests.cs, KS3_4PreflightTests.cs, KS3_5ImportBridgeTests.cs. PROCESS HYGIENE (traps 3, 12). A second conductor run may share this machine. Never kill a conductor.exe, conductor-face.exe or stray dotnet by pid without checking its command line with Get-CimInstance Win32_Process; stopping an orphaned `dotnet test` host is sanctioned only after that check proves it belongs to this repo. Never kill a conductor process, yours or anyone's.

Commit per checkpoint with the repo's trailer convention and push feat/karvansara. If you move a file the run depends on (the plan's readOrder target, the tracker, a template), update the plan and reload it in the same checkpoint.
